$comment: Canonical design tokens for JourneySync. This file is the single source of
truth for every value the website and the Android app must agree on.
Do not hand-edit the generated files. Run `npm run tokens` after changing
anything here; `npm test` runs `npm run tokens:check`, which fails if a
generated file has drifted from this source.
The two platforms deliberately keep their own vocabulary: the web calls the
page background `--paper` and the Android code calls the same colour
SURFACE. Renaming either would churn thousands of call sites for no user
benefit, so each token carries explicit per-platform names instead. The
value is shared; only the label differs.
`web` or `android` may be null when a token is not yet adopted on that
platform. That is a real gap worth closing, not a licence to hardcode.

navy.use: Darkest brand surface: sidebar, status banner, sign-in intro panel.

navyRaised.use: Raised element sitting on top of navy.

ink.use: Primary text on light surfaces, and unselected map pins.

faint.use: Tertiary text, one step lighter than muted.

paper.use: Card and sheet surface. Also the Android status bar backdrop.

coral.use: Brand accent, selected state, and the delayed-flight signal.

coralPressed.use: Pressed state for coral buttons. Currently unused: coral moved to warnings and destructive actions only, and those surfaces have no pressed variant yet.

success.use: On-time and settled, on a light background.

successOnDark.use: The same on-time signal placed on navy. A separate token on purpose: the two are not interchangeable, because each is chosen for contrast against its own background.

warning.use: Caution state, short of an outright delay.

danger.use: Destructive actions: delete an expense, a wallet document, a traveler.

purple.use: Secondary categorical accent. Renamed from --accent on the web when the interactive accent moved to blue; the Android name was already PURPLE.

accent.use: Interactive accent. Same value as blue, kept as its own name because the UI refers to the role, not the hue. Android reads BLUE directly.

accentPressed.use: Pressed state for the interactive accent.

accentSoft.use: Tinted fill behind the interactive accent.

card.use: Corner radius for cards and the embedded trip map.
